items.title: Nasdaq gains 0.5% to close at a record 27,244 on Tuesday
items.content: The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.5% to a fresh record close of 27,244 on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 also firm near all-time highs. Losses in Cisco (-4.50%), JPMorgan (-3.35%) and American Express (-2.62%) were offset by Amgen (+4.33%), Home Depot (+2.74%) and Honeywell (+2.58%). (Report dated 2026-09-22 US session.)

items.title: Nasdaq jumps 2% to close at a record, buoyed by surge in AI stocks, as well as cooling oil and yields
items.content: The Nasdaq Composite posted its first record close since June, powered by a broad AI-led chip rally. Oil prices and Treasury yields cooled at the same time, easing pressure on growth valuations. Published ~3 hours before collection.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Sept. 21: Tech strength powers Nasdaq to record close
items.content: Semiconductor stocks surged on AI demand while Bitcoin topped $87,000, offsetting energy sector weakness. Confirms the AI-hardware bid is broadening even as oil-related names lag.

items.title: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index closes 0.18% higher
items.content: Hong Kong's benchmark Hang Seng Index ended Tuesday up 0.18% at 25,087.75. The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index rose 0.28% to 8,362.6 and the Hang Seng Tech Index rose 0.34% to 4,438.21. Index is back above the 25,000 psychological level.

items.title: Hang Seng tests 25,050 resistance at cloud top; stuck below 24,981 in no-trade zone
items.content: Technical read: HSI is pressing the 25,050 cloud-top resistance while trapped below the 24,981 support-turned-resistance. A clean break of 25,050 opens further upside; failure keeps the index range-bound.

items.title: Oil price today: crude snaps 4-day fall, hovers near $101 on potential US-Iran talks
items.content: Brent crude futures for November rose 74 cents (+0.75%) to around $101 a barrel, snapping a four-session slide, amid hints of potential US-Iran talks. Trading Economics separately shows Brent at 98.47 USD/bbl (-1.87%) on Sept 22 — CFD vs futures spread signals a volatile, headline-driven oil tape.

items.title: 2026 Iran war: brief operational standoff, US clearing Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes
items.content: The Iran-US conflict entered a brief operational standoff in August 2026 after fierce July combat, marked by a sharp decline in direct kinetic engagements and an end to Iranian strikes on Gulf Arab states. US forces continue clearing crucial shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz. Tensions trace back to failed Geneva nuclear talks.

items.title: Despite June MoU to reopen Hormuz, Iran seeks hegemonic control and transit fees
items.content: Despite the June 2026 memorandum of understanding meant to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the Iran war, Iran has sought to assert hegemonic control over the strait and eventually collect fees on ships passing through — keeping the energy risk premium structurally elevated.

items.title: Geopolitical risk is the new normal — Asia input shortages from Strait disruption
items.content: Asia faces shortages in fertilizer (food supply), chemicals (tech hardware) and plastics (autos, pharma), sparking double-digit price increases for these inputs within weeks. Even a rapid reopening of the Strait could leave an 'air pocket' as supply chains normalize slowly.

items.title: China stocks mixed, Hong Kong shares edge higher as AI weakness weighs
items.content: Mainland stocks traded mixed as AI and semiconductor shares fell — CSI AI Index -1.2%, STAR50 -0.9% — while banking stocks rose on defensive rotation. Contrasts with the US AI-led record rally, showing Asia is lagging the chip trade.

items.title: US PCE inflation: headline steady at 3.7%, core at 3.3% (latest reading)
items.content: Latest annual headline PCE inflation held at 3.7% (above 3.6% expected) while core PCE held at 3.3%, matching expectations. Fed's preferred gauge remains well above the 2% target, keeping the 'higher-for-longer' debate alive ahead of the next PCE print.

items.title: Earnings calendar week of Sept 21-25: 18 reports Thursday, nearly empty Friday
items.content: No market-moving mega-cap results this week; Thursday Sept 24 peaks the schedule with 18 earnings while Friday Sept 25 is essentially empty. Focus shifts to macro data (PCE, GDP) rather than single-name earnings.
